title: Perseus: The Reckoning
subtitle: Back to Seriphus — the promised gift delivered at last

How is the original oracle fulfilled?

main.excerpt: he entered the palace, where Polydectes had gathered his friends, and with averted face he showed the Gorgon's head; and all who beheld it were turned to stone

narrativeBlocks.title: Home to an occupied island
narrativeBlocks.body: Perseus returns to Seriphus to find his mother and foster-father hiding at the altars — Polydectes, assuming him dead, has been pressing Danae in earnest.

narrativeBlocks.title: The promised gift, delivered
narrativeBlocks.body: Perseus walks into the palace where Polydectes has gathered his court — and produces the promised wedding-gift: he shows the Gorgon's head with averted face, and every man who sees it turns to stone where he sits.

narrativeBlocks.title: Argos and the fulfilled oracle
narrativeBlocks.body: He then goes home to Argos — and the original prophecy finally lands. Competing in games elsewhere, he throws a discus that swerves and strikes an old spectator dead: his grandfather Acrisius, the man who set the chest adrift.

narrativeBlocks.title: An inheritance refused
narrativeBlocks.body: Perseus cannot comfortably rule the kingdom he gained by killing its king — so he swaps Argos for Tiryns and founds Mycenae, the very city whose kings will later field Agamemnon.

narrativeBlocks.title: Prophecies don't miss
narrativeBlocks.body: The arc closes the way it opened: Acrisius's every evasive move — the chamber, the chest — only ensured the grandson would arrive with the skills, the tools, and the occasion to fulfil the oracle. Fate completes itself on a stray discus.

quiz.prompt: How does Perseus deal with Polydectes on his return?

choices.text: He duels Polydectes before the people
He has him arrested for treason
He shows the Gorgon's head in the crowded palace — the king and his court are turned to stone

quiz.explanation: The 'wedding gift' is delivered literally — the trap is repaid with the trophy it demanded.

quiz.prompt: How does the oracle about Acrisius finally come true?

choices.text: Perseus kills him on sight in Argos
He dies in the palace when the head is shown
He is executed for setting the chest adrift
At funeral games, Perseus's discus swerves and kills an old spectator — his grandfather

quiz.explanation: The prophecy is fulfilled by accident — the classic Greek verdict that fate cannot be dodged.
